ArubaQosGlobal_QSchedProfileConfig.description: Combined QoS queue- and schedule-profile global pairing.

q-profile.description:
Queue profile to apply in combination with the specified
schedule profile. Queue profiles must first be configured using the
aruba-qos-queue yang model, and must be valid for the platform to
which the profile is being applied.

Queue profiles cannot be modified while they are applied. The number
of queues and queue ID values must also match those in the paired
schedule profile. If an applied queue profile is modified, the
configuration will be rejected. To apply the modified queue profile,
follow the following sequence of operations:

1. If sched-profile in aruba-qos-global is set to DEFAULT, set
q-profile to DEFAULT. Otherwise, remove both q-profile and
sched-profile. This will cause the factory-default profiles
to be applied.
2. For PVOS devices, ensure that the traffic-template leaf is not
set to the same profile as the queue-profile being modified. If it
is, delete the traffic-template by setting the traffic-template
leaf to null.
3. Modify the queue profile.
4. If both q-profile and sched-profile were removed in step 1,
apply them again together in the same transaction. If q-profile
was set to DEFAULT in step 1, apply only the queue profile.
5. For PVOS devices, if the traffic template was removed as part of
this process, apply it again after the queue profile
has been modified.

oneOf.x-typeDescription:
The QoS factory-default profile definition. This can be
used to apply default Queue and/or Schedule profiles.

sched-profile.description:
Schedule profile to apply in combination with the specified
queue profile. Schedule profiles must first be configured using the
aruba-qos-schedule yang model, and must be valid for the platform to
which the profile is being applied. The number of queues and queue ID
values must also match those in the paired queue profile.

contain alphanumeric characters, periods, underscores, and hyphens

been detected as blocked. The queue will resume normal operation

triggered.

pool.description:
Pool for lossless traffic. On some platforms, at least one QoS memory
pool must be configured before any interface flow-control features will
take effect. For Link-Level Flow Control (LLFC), either default pool 1
should be created or the created pool should match the llfc pool ID that
will be specified when flow-control is configured for an interface. For
Priority Flow Control (PFC), the memory pool(s) should be created and
then the priorities to be flow-controlled should be mapped to the
desired memory pool(s).

headroom-size.description:
The headroom buffer size in kilobytes. Headroom size must be
specified for every configured memory pool.

priority.description:
List of priorities to be mapped to this pool for use by the interface
Priority Flow Control (PFC) feature.

items.description:
List of priorities to be mapped to this pool for use by the interface
Priority Flow Control (PFC) feature.

size.description:
The percentage of packet buffer memory to be allocated to this
memory pool in integer or decimal formats. The amount should be
large enough to accommodate the headroom pool, which is also
allocated from this same memory pool. Size must be specified for
every configured memory pool.
